title: A Extraction for the Cover
premise: Casper Villalobos, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent years laundering her own past into a spotless identity, is summoned when a voiceprint—her own voice, recorded years ago and thought destroyed—unlocks a server in Malta holding proof that a transnational 'clean money' fund is a front for state-sponsored assassination. Hunted by the assassin whose kills she's tracing, betrayed by the mentor who kept her go-bag packed for exactly this day, Casper must smuggle the truth through three governments' jurisdictions while confronting that the server also contains evidence of her own buried crimes. In the end she trades her polished lie—her real name, her real record—to a journalist and a weary INTERPOL agent who have become her found family, burning her old identity to light the fuse that brings the fund down.
about_author: Elodie Reyes is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade inside the quiet machinery of international finance before trading spreadsheets for sentences. She writes thrillers about people whose paperwork is more dangerous than their pistols, from a rotating series of borrowed desks.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Test
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. In Lisbon, Casper runs her monthly ritual: repack the go-bag, rehearse the cover story, audit her own clean-money life for cracks. A routine case file on a shell fund nags at her. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a woman whose identity is a performance she can never stop giving.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A Maltese data broker's dead-man switch fires: a server unlocks to a voiceprint sample labeled with Casper's name—a recording she made nine years ago and believed erased. Her mentor, Aldous Wren, tells her to ignore it. She can't. Emotional beat: dread as the past knocks politely instead of kicking the door.

chapters.title: Valletta, After Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper flies to Malta under a work pretext and meets the broker's widow, who hands over a drive fragment and one warning: someone else has been asking. That night a man watches her hotel from a café, unhurried, professional. Emotional beat: the first cold drop of real fear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Waits
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya Sarn, the assassin. We meet him mid-contract, methodical and oddly gentle, reviewing a kill list generated by the fund's algorithm. Casper's name appears twice—as witness, as target. He requests more time. Emotional beat: chilling calm; evil as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Back home, Casper traces the Meridian Sovereign Fund's flows and finds the impossible: every dollar spotless, every trail deliberately beautiful. Only someone inside designed it. Suspicion lands uncomfortably close to Wren. Emotional beat: professional awe curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Confrontation with Wren, who admits he built the fund's architecture years ago as an intelligence tool and insists it was hijacked. He reveals he kept her old recording as insurance—on her, not for her. Emotional beat: the found-family myth cracks; loyalty becomes leverage.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper maps the jurisdictional maze: US Treasury, Europol, and a Singaporean regulator each hold a piece of the truth, and each would bury it to protect their own exposure. She realizes no single agency can be trusted with everything. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: INTERPOL, Second Desk
chapters.summary: POV: Amara Diallo. INTERPOL agent Amara Diallo, stuck on a financial-crimes backwater desk, notices the same impossible cleanliness in three unrelated files. She flags Casper's travel pattern. Emotional beat: lonely competence recognizing its mirror across a continent.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper and Amara make cautious contact in Lyon, trading half-truths over bad coffee. Amara offers channels, not protection. Casper offers fragments, not trust. Both know they're being watched. Emotional beat: the fragile first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: The Widow's Tape
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The drive fragment decrypts partially: audio of a fund board meeting approving a 'termination protocol.' Among the voices, Casper hears Wren's—and her own, reading terms aloud years ago. Emotional beat: horror of complicity; her voice used as a key to murder.

chapters.title: Sarn Closes
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya Sarn. Sarn eliminates the fund's former auditor in Rotterdam and studies Casper's file until she feels less like a target than a puzzle. He delays again, citing anomalies. His handler grows suspicious. Emotional beat: the assassin developing a conscience-shaped crack.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper's credentials are revoked mid-investigation; her accounts frozen by someone using her own compliance playbook against her. Wren warns her to run. Instead she goes dark, taking only the go-bag. Emotional beat: the polished lie finally failing; freedom in losing everything.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Hiding in Amara's cousin's apartment in Marseille, Casper and Amara plan the split: three copies of the evidence, three governments, staggered release so no one can kill the story quietly. Emotional beat: two strangers becoming a unit under pressure.

chapters.title: Singapore Trap
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The Singapore handoff is ambushed—the regulator was flipped weeks ago. Casper escapes with the copy but loses her courier, Devi, who bought her seconds with her life. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; the cost of the mission made flesh.

chapters.title: What Sarn Knows
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya Sarn. Ordered to finish Casper, Sarn instead sends her an encrypted message: the board meeting tape is incomplete, and the missing section names the fund's true principal—a sitting official. He wants out, and she's his exit. Emotional beat: enemy becoming reluctant ally.

chapters.title: The Devil's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Meeting Sarn in Trieste, Casper verifies his fragment against her own. The full ledger implicates a deputy secretary-general—and shows Wren approved the termination protocol personally. Emotional beat: the last illusion about her mentor dying cleanly.

chapters.title: Wren's Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Wren intercepts them, gun drawn, arguing he contained the program to prevent worse. Casper records his confession, then lets him face the fund's own cleaners rather than pull the trigger herself. They escape as he doesn't. Emotional beat: mercy and ruthlessness indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The fund triggers a global data purge; backups die hourly. Casper, Amara, and Sarn race to place all three copies before the window closes—Washington, The Hague, Singapore—splitting up for the first time. Emotional beat: ticking-clock terror fused with trust.

chapters.title: The Hague Handoff
chapters.summary: POV: Amara Diallo. Amara delivers her copy through a prosecutor she once distrusted, then walks into an ambush meant for Casper, buying time with badge and nerve. Wounded but alive, she confirms the chain holds. Emotional beat: sacrifice proving the family real.

chapters.title: Terminal Velocity
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. At Changi, Sarn's handlers corner them; Sarn turns himself in loudly to create chaos, shouting the deputy's name where cameras will hear. Casper gets the final copy airborne to Treasury. Emotional beat: climax—truth escaping by inches, paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Weeks later, the fund collapses, arrests ripple across four countries, and Casper testifies under her real name—the one she buried nine years ago—surrendering her old crimes as the price of the truth. Amara waits outside. Emotional beat: identity surrendered and self finally claimed.

chapters.title: A New Bag, Barely Packed
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Epilogue: Casper unpacks the go-bag for good, keeps only the voice recorder, and takes a teaching post training investigators to read money like confessions. A postcard arrives from an unknown prison—Sarn, alive, one line: 'Still waiting.' Emotional beat: hard-won peace with a door left open.
